summary: SSE/Websocket streaming stalls mid-token due to edge-proxy chunk coalescing and worker starvation
description:
Issue summary:
On 2026-03-12 we started receiving multiple customer reports (first from Acme Health) where SSE and websocket streaming sessions stall mid-generation — often while a token is still being emitted (client sees a partial token and then silence). Impact: production streaming sessions for some dedicated customers experience mid-generation stalls causing client timeouts and degraded UX.

Impact:
- Intermittent mid-token stalls on long-running chat generations (20-60s).
- Affects ~2-4% of long-form streaming requests for affected customers in us-east; smaller spike observed in eu-west.
- Customers experience client-side timeouts and reopen attempts which sometimes succeed.

Environment:
- Prod serving behind the edge-nginx fleet in us-east (edge-proxy for dedicated customers).
- Affected routes: /v1/chat/stream, /v1/generate/stream with adaptive batching enabled for throughput optimization.

Observed behavior:
- Client receives partial token bytes then connection goes quiet (no FIN/RST). Socket remains ESTABLISHED; upstream logs show worker is still assigned to request but not emitting chunks.
- Internal metrics show concurrent request queueing and worker slot exhaustion around the time stalls occur.

Expected behavior:
- Continuous streaming of chunks until generation completes, with keepalive heartbeats preventing silent stalls.

Attachments/logs:
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streaming/streaming-slo?orgId=1&from=now-1h&to=now (spike visible 2026-03-12 16:05-16:25 UTC)
- Kibana traces: https://kibana.redwood.ai/app/discover#/?_a=(query:(match:...)) (sample trace id: trace-20260312-5b7a)
- Support thread: Slack #support (thread ts: 1649875600.12345)
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a dedicated account (Acme Health) in us-east with adaptive batching enabled.
2) Start a streaming chat request with ~6k token context and request streaming via SSE or websocket.
3) Observe that after a period of emitted tokens (~15-40s) the stream becomes silent without connection close and no final event delivered.
4) Re-running the same request sometimes completes successfully; failure rate ~2-4% on observed windows.
logs: edge-nginx error_log: keepalive_pool_full, coalesced_write_event on socket 192.0.2.77:54321
serving-runtime INFO: worker-27: starting generation job id=gen-9a3b; kv_cache_hits=0; batch_size=1
serving-runtime WARN: adaptive_batcher delayed flush: queue_depth=62; last_flush=1270ms
proxy-trace: upstream_read_timeout not hit; connection persisted; no RST
investigation_notes: Support triage (Priya): Collected logs from customer, validated reproducible pattern for long-context streaming under high concurrency.

SRE (Marco): Observed edge-nginx keepalive pool saturation correlated with time windows. Nginx pooling occasionally coalesces small writes into larger TCP segments; combined with adaptive batching delaying flushes this can lead to head-of-line blocking inside worker write buffers.

Eng (Taylor): Serving runtime shows worker is still active (not crashed) but last_write timestamp stops after a partial chunk. The runtime flush path defers small chunk flushes to amortize kernel calls; when edge proxy buffers + coalescing occurs, the TCP send buffer does not actually transmit until net stack decides, resulting in perceived silence at client even though upstream app hasn't signaled end.

Hypothesis: Interaction between adaptive batching (which intentionally delays small-chunk flushes), edge-nginx keepalive and buffer coalescing, and a limited streaming worker pool causes effective worker starvation and mid-token silence. TL;DR: small-chunk buffering + proxy coalescing = silent period.
Observed amplification under burst load and when keepalive re-use leads to many streams multiplexed on same upstream connections.
comments: 2026-03-12 Priya Nair (Support): Affected customer (Acme Health) reports multiple mid-stream stalls yesterday afternoon. Collection of SDK trace, sample request IDs, and client timings attached. Asking for engineering investigation.
2026-03-12 Marco Delgado (SRE): Reproduced locally with dedicated config and load-generator; replicated 2/50 failures within 1 hour. Noted nginx keepalive_pool_full events.

2026-03-13 Taylor Kim (Serving Eng): Instrumented runtime path; added debug logging for flush/flush_delay and confirmed flush delayed beyond 1s in failing traces. Opening a quick PR to add explicit chunk flush on streaming routes.

2026-03-13 Marco Delgado (SRE): Temporary mitigation applied at edge: increased proxy_buffer_size and keepalive pool from 64->256 and tuned proxy_http_version to 1.1 for streaming routes. Also increased upstream_read_timeout to 120s. Customer reports reduced rate of stalls for initial window.

2026-03-14 Taylor Kim (Serving Eng): Merged PR #1289 to force flush on streaming-chunk boundary and added per-stream flush timeout (200ms). Scheduled controlled rollout to 10% of streaming requests to validate impact.

2026-03-14 Priya Nair (Support): Informed Acme Health of mitigation and scheduled follow-up for 2026-03-16 to confirm full resolution. Customer appreciated rapid response but asked for root-cause report.
resolution: Workaround and mitigation: SRE increased edge keepalive pool and adjusted proxy buffering; Eng deployed change to force periodic flushes on streaming chunks and introduced per-stream flush timeout. Root cause (working hypothesis): interaction of adaptive batching delayed flushes with edge-proxy TCP coalescing and limited worker pool leading to transient silent periods mid-token. Next steps: monitor rollout, further harden batching logic to avoid delaying first N chunks, add per-route proxy config for streaming, and create a postmortem if residual error rates exceed 0.5% over 24h.

2026-03-14: In Progress - PR merged and canary rollout started (10%)
